title: Grade 4 ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — 7.2 Earliest Converts in Islam

PAGE 1: Overview

OVERVIEW
========

When the Prophet (S.A.W) began to call people to Islam, a small group believed him at once. This sub-strand is about three of the earliest: Khadijah (R.A.), Ali (R.A.) and Abubakar (R.A.). You will learn who they were, how they supported his mission, and why Muslims still honour that support.

## Strand 7.0: History of Islam
Sub-strand 7.2: Earliest Converts in Islam
Suggested lessons: 3

## Learning outcomes
By the end of the sub-strand, the learner should be able to:
a) identify the earliest converts to Islam
b) explain the role played by the earliest converts to Islam
c) appreciate the role played by earliest converts to the development of Islam

## What this sub-strand covers
• Khadija (R.A.)
• Ali (R.A.)
• Abubakar (R.A.)

## Key inquiry questions
1. What role did the earliest converts play in the Prophet’s mission?

## Core competencies
• Communication and collaboration: the skill of listening, speaking and writing as learners identify the qualities that led Khadija (R.A) to propose to marry the Prophet (e.g. trustworthy, honesty, hardworking), in pairs/groups, and write the points in their notebook
• Learning to learn: the skill of sharing learnt knowledge as learners listen to a resource person discussing the role of Khadija in the life of Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W). (e.g. First person to accept Islam, moral support, all his children were born by Khadija apart from Ibrahim, her wealth support).

## Values
• Respect: etiquette enhanced as learners listen attentively to a resource person discussing the role of Khadija in the life of Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W).

## Pertinent and contemporary issues
• Citizenship: Nationalism by volunteering in Islamic activities in the community.

## Links to other learning areas
• Social Studies as learners learn on personalities and their role in the country or different community development.

## Source
• KICD Grade 4 Islamic Religious Education Curriculum Design (Revised 2024) — Strand 7.0 History of Islam, Sub-strand 7.2 Earliest Converts in Islam
• The design names Khadijah (R.A.), Ali (R.A.) and Abubakar (R.A.), and notes Khadijah as the first to accept Islam, her moral support and wealth, and that all the Prophet's children except Ibrahim were born to her

PAGE 2: Lesson 1: Khadijah (R.A.), the first to believe

LESSON 1: KHADIJAH (R.A.), THE FIRST TO BELIEVE
===============================================

## What you will learn
• Name Khadijah (R.A.) among the earliest converts.
• Explain the support she gave to the Prophet (S.A.W).
• State qualities that made her trust him.

Curriculum outcomes: a) identify the earliest converts to Islam; b) explain the role played by the earliest converts to Islam; c) appreciate the role played by earliest converts to the development of Islam

## Introduction
Before the message spread through Makkah, it was believed inside one house. The first person to accept Islam was Khadijah bint Khuwaylid (R.A.), the wife of the Prophet (S.A.W).

## Notes
### Who she was
Khadijah (R.A.) was a respected woman of Makkah, known for her trade and her good sense. She employed Muhammad (S.A.W) to take goods for trade. She heard of his honesty, trustworthiness and hard work. The people already called him Al-Amin, the Trustworthy. She proposed marriage, and he accepted. Their home became the first place where Islam was believed.

The three earliest converts you will study are Khadijah (R.A.), Ali (R.A.) and Abubakar (R.A.). Khadijah is the first of them, and the first person to accept the message.

### Her role in the mission
- She was the first person to accept Islam. When he came from Cave Hira afraid, she believed him and comforted him.
- She gave moral support. She stood by him when others later mocked the new message.
- She gave material support. She used her wealth to help the mission and to care for the family so that he could carry the message.
- She was the mother of his children, except Ibrahim, who was born later to Mariya (R.A.). Their daughters include Zaynab, Ruqayyah, Umm Kulthum and Fatimah (R.A.).

### What we appreciate
Khadijah shows that supporting Islam can mean believing first, speaking kindly, and spending wealth in a good cause. A learner appreciates her by telling her story truthfully and by copying the loyalty she showed: stand by what is right, and do not abandon a good person when he is under pressure.

## Key words
• convert — a person who accepts Islam
• Al-Amin — the Trustworthy
• moral support — encouragement, comfort and loyalty
• material support — help with money, food or other goods

## Worked examples

### Example 1
A classmate says Khadijah only became Muslim because she was rich. What is a fairer answer from the story?

Working:
1. She proposed marriage because of his honesty, trustworthiness and hard work.
2. She believed him after Cave Hira because she knew his character, and then she used her wealth to help.

Answer: She believed because of his character and the truth of the message. Her wealth was a means of support after she believed, not the reason for her faith.

## Activity: The earliest three, beginning with Khadijah
You will need: Course book or reference material, Exercise book
1. In pairs, mention the earliest converts studied in this sub-strand: Khadijah (R.A.), Ali (R.A.) and Abubakar (R.A.). Write the three names.
2. Read the story of Khadijah and list the qualities that led her to trust the Prophet: trustworthy, honest and hardworking.
3. Write the roles she played: first to accept Islam, moral support, and support with her wealth.
4. Share one role with the class.

## Practice
1. Who was the first person to accept Islam?
2. Name the three earliest converts studied in this sub-strand.
3. Which qualities led Khadijah to propose marriage to Muhammad (S.A.W)?
4. State two ways Khadijah supported the Prophet's mission.

## Summary
• Khadijah (R.A.) was the first person to accept Islam.
• She trusted the Prophet because he was honest, trustworthy and hardworking.
• She supported the mission with comfort and with her wealth.

### Answers to practice
1. Khadijah (R.A.).
2. Khadijah (R.A.), Ali (R.A.) and Abubakar (R.A.).
3. He was trustworthy, honest and hardworking.
4. Any two: she was the first to believe, she comforted him, she gave moral support, she supported him with her wealth.

PAGE 3: Lesson 2: Ali (R.A.), the young cousin who believed

LESSON 2: ALI (R.A.), THE YOUNG COUSIN WHO BELIEVED
===================================================

## What you will learn
• Identify Ali (R.A.) as one of the earliest converts.
• Describe the support he gave while he was still young.
• State one lesson from his loyalty.

Curriculum outcomes: a) identify the earliest converts to Islam; b) explain the role played by the earliest converts to Islam; c) appreciate the role played by earliest converts to the development of Islam

## Introduction
Islam was not accepted only by adults. A boy who lived in the Prophet's house saw the message from the first days and believed it. That boy was Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A.).

## Notes
### Who Ali was
Ali (R.A.) was the son of Abu Talib, the Prophet's uncle. Abu Talib had a large family. The Prophet (S.A.W) took Ali into his own home so that he could help his uncle, and Ali grew up close to him and to Khadijah (R.A.). He was still a child when Islam began.

He is remembered among the earliest converts, together with Khadijah (R.A.) and Abubakar (R.A.). Muslims speak of him as the young person in that first circle who accepted the message early and stayed with it.

### His role
- He accepted Islam while young, so the first community included a child, not only grown people.
- He lived with the Prophet (S.A.W) and saw his worship and his honesty every day. His belief came from that closeness.
- He gave loyalty. As the mission became harder in Makkah, Ali remained on the side of the Prophet.
- He is remembered for courage. Even as a young Muslim he did not leave the Messenger when many people of Makkah opposed the new faith.

The design of this study asks learners to notice that the earliest Muslims gave moral support, and some risked their safety. Ali's story shows a young person's share in that support.

### A lesson for learners
Age is not a barrier to faith. A Grade 4 learner cannot copy every later event in Ali's life, but can copy the early lesson: when you know the truth, accept it, stay loyal, and do not be ashamed of worship. Courage at this age looks like telling the truth, standing by a classmate who is being mocked for praying, and keeping up swalah.

## Key words
• Ali (R.A.) — the cousin of the Prophet (S.A.W), son of Abu Talib, and one of the earliest Muslims
• Abu Talib — the Prophet's uncle and the father of Ali
• loyalty — staying faithful to someone, especially in a hard time

## Worked examples

### Example 1
Some older boys laugh at a Grade 4 learner who leaves the game to pray. How does Ali's early faith guide the learner?

Working:
1. Ali accepted Islam as a child and stayed loyal.
2. The learner can pray without shame and speak calmly.

Answer: He or she should go to pray, without insulting the others, and not abandon the practice because of laughter.

## Activity: Story of Ali
You will need: Course book or a short story read by a resource person or from a digital device
1. Listen to the story of Ali (R.A.).
2. Write who he was: cousin of the Prophet, son of Abu Talib, raised in the Prophet's home.
3. Write two roles he played in the early mission.
4. Tell the story in your own words to a partner.

## Practice
1. Whose son was Ali (R.A.), and how was he related to the Prophet (S.A.W)?
2. Why was Ali living in the Prophet's household?
3. State two ways Ali supported the early mission.
4. What can a young learner copy from Ali's early faith?

## Summary
• Ali (R.A.) was the Prophet's young cousin and one of the earliest Muslims.
• He grew up in the Prophet's home and remained loyal.
• His story shows that a child can believe and stand by the truth.

### Answers to practice
1. He was the son of Abu Talib, the Prophet's uncle, so he was the Prophet's cousin.
2. The Prophet (S.A.W) took him in to help Abu Talib, who had a large family, and Ali grew up close to him.
3. Any two: he accepted Islam while young, he stayed loyal, he lived close to the Prophet and supported him, he showed courage when people opposed the message.
4. Accepting the truth while young, staying loyal, and not being ashamed of worship.

PAGE 4: Lesson 3: Abubakar (R.A.) and what we learn from the earliest Muslims

LESSON 3: ABUBAKAR (R.A.) AND WHAT WE LEARN FROM THE EARLIEST MUSLIMS
============================================================

## What you will learn
• Identify Abubakar (R.A.) as one of the earliest converts.
• Explain how he supported the Prophet's mission.
• Appreciate the work of the earliest Muslims and name one way to follow it.

Curriculum outcomes: a) identify the earliest converts to Islam; b) explain the role played by the earliest converts to Islam; c) appreciate the role played by earliest converts to the development of Islam

## Introduction
A close friend can either pull you back or walk forward with you. Abubakar ibn Abi Quhafah (R.A.) heard the message from his friend and believed it without delay.

## Notes
### Who Abubakar was
Abubakar (R.A.) was a close friend of the Prophet (S.A.W) even before Islam. He was known as a gentle and truthful man of Makkah. When the Prophet told him of the revelation, he accepted Islam at once. He is counted with Khadijah (R.A.) and Ali (R.A.) among the earliest converts, and he is remembered as the first free man outside the Prophet's household to believe.

### His role
- He believed immediately. He did not wait to see if the chiefs of Makkah would agree.
- He gave moral support. His calm trust strengthened the Prophet (S.A.W).
- He gave material support. He spent his wealth in the path of Islam.
- He used that wealth to free slaves who were being persecuted for their faith. The freeing of Bilal ibn Rabah (R.A.) is the best-known example. Bilal was tortured for saying that Allah is One, and Abubakar bought his freedom.
- He called other people to Islam and stood with the Prophet when belief was costly.

The earliest converts, taken together, gave the mission its first believers, its first encouragement, its first money, and lives that were ready to bear hardship.

### Appreciating their role
Islam reached later generations because these people held the message at the start. Appreciation is not only a poster of their names. It is:

- Telling the story accurately
- Making dua for them when we remember them
- Volunteering in good Islamic work in the community, such as helping at the mosque or supporting a classmate
- Believing what is true even when friends delay

Khadijah, Ali and Abubakar had different ages and different kinds of help. Each help was needed. A learner's help today may be small, but sincere support of the deen continues their example.

## Key words
• Abubakar (R.A.) — the close friend of the Prophet (S.A.W) and one of the first men to accept Islam
• Bilal (R.A.) — an early Muslim who was freed from slavery; he later gave the call to prayer
• persecution — cruel treatment because of one's faith

## Worked examples

### Example 1
A learner has a little money saved. He wants to copy Abubakar (R.A.). What is a suitable way at Grade 4, and what would not fit?

Working:
1. Abubakar spent wealth to help people harmed for their faith.
2. A child can give a small sadaqah or help someone in need, with a parent's guidance. He cannot copy every adult action.

Answer: He can give a small amount of charity or help a person in need. Showing off, or taking money that is not his, would not follow Abubakar.

## Activity: Roles of the earliest converts
You will need: Notebook, A story of Abubakar (R.A.) from a resource person, course book or digital device
1. Listen to the story of Abubakar (R.A.).
2. Make a table with three names: Khadijah, Ali and Abubakar. Under each name write one role in the Prophet's mission.
3. Discuss, in pairs, why their support mattered at the beginning of Islam.
4. Write one way you can volunteer in a good activity at home, school or the mosque.

## Practice
1. What was the relationship between Abubakar (R.A.) and the Prophet (S.A.W) before Islam?
2. How did Abubakar respond when he heard the message?
3. How did Abubakar help Bilal (R.A.)?
4. Give one way a learner can appreciate the earliest converts.

## Summary
• Abubakar (R.A.) believed at once and supported the mission with loyalty and wealth.
• He freed Muslims who were persecuted, including Bilal (R.A.).
• Khadijah, Ali and Abubakar each gave support that helped Islam begin.

### Answers to practice
1. They were close friends.
2. He accepted Islam at once.
3. He spent his money to free Bilal, who was being persecuted for his faith.
4. Any one: tell their story truthfully, make dua for them, support good Islamic work, or stand by the truth.
pages.quiz:
REVISION QUIZ — 7.2 EARLIEST CONVERTS IN ISLAM
========================================

Answer all the questions, then mark yourself on the Answers tab.

1. Who was the first person to accept Islam?
   A. Abubakar (R.A.)
   B. Khadijah (R.A.)
   C. Bilal (R.A.)
   D. Waraqah

2. Which three are the earliest converts studied here?
   A. Khadijah, Ali and Abubakar
   B. Musa, Isa and Yusuf
   C. Bilal, Salman and Suhayb only
   D. Abu Talib, Abu Lahab and Waraqah

3. Why did Khadijah trust Muhammad (S.A.W) before Islam?
   A. lazy and proud
   B. trustworthy, honest and hardworking
   C. a king
   D. unknown in Makkah

4. Which support did Khadijah give?
   A. She opposed the message
   B. She comforted him and supported him with her wealth
   C. She left Makkah before believing
   D. She refused to listen

5. Ali (R.A.) was…
   A. a stranger from Taif
   B. the Prophet's cousin, son of Abu Talib
   C. the angel Jibril
   D. a leader who rejected Islam

6. What does Ali's early acceptance teach a child?

7. Abubakar (R.A.) is remembered as…
   A. a friend who believed at once and spent his wealth for Islam
   B. a man who refused the message
   C. the angel of the cave
   D. an opponent from Taif

8. Why is Bilal (R.A.) linked to Abubakar in this lesson?
   A. Abubakar persecuted him
   B. Abubakar freed him from slavery
   C. they never met
   D. Bilal rejected Islam

9. How did the earliest converts help the mission?

10. A learner appreciates their role by…
   A. forgetting their names
   B. telling the story truthfully and supporting good work
   C. mocking people who pray
   D. changing the story
pages.answers:
ANSWERS — 7.2 EARLIEST CONVERTS IN ISLAM
========================================

1. B. Khadijah (R.A.)
   Khadijah (R.A.) believed the Prophet when he received the first revelation.

2. A. Khadijah, Ali and Abubakar
   This sub-strand names Khadijah (R.A.), Ali (R.A.) and Abubakar (R.A.).

3. B. trustworthy, honest and hardworking
   Those qualities led her to propose marriage. People called him Al-Amin.

4. B. She comforted him and supported him with her wealth
   Her role was moral support and material support, and she was the first believer.

5. B. the Prophet's cousin, son of Abu Talib
   He grew up close to the Prophet and accepted Islam while young.

6. A young person can believe the truth and stay loyal to it.
   He was still a child when he entered Islam.

7. A. a friend who believed at once and spent his wealth for Islam
   He gave both moral and material support.

8. B. Abubakar freed him from slavery
   Abubakar used his money to free Bilal, who was tortured for his faith.

9. Believing first, giving moral and material support, and bearing hardship for the message.
   Their faith, encouragement, wealth and courage carried the mission at the start.

10. B. telling the story truthfully and supporting good work
   Appreciation is shown by truthfulness and by continuing good Islamic effort.

studyPages.title: Lesson 3: Abubakar (R.A.) and what we learn from the earliest Muslims
studyPages.body:
LESSON 3: ABUBAKAR (R.A.) AND WHAT WE LEARN FROM THE EARLIEST MUSLIMS
============================================================

## What you will learn
• Identify Abubakar (R.A.) as one of the earliest converts.
• Explain how he supported the Prophet's mission.
• Appreciate the work of the earliest Muslims and name one way to follow it.

Curriculum outcomes: a) identify the earliest converts to Islam; b) explain the role played by the earliest converts to Islam; c) appreciate the role played by earliest converts to the development of Islam

## Introduction
A close friend can either pull you back or walk forward with you. Abubakar ibn Abi Quhafah (R.A.) heard the message from his friend and believed it without delay.

## Notes
### Who Abubakar was
Abubakar (R.A.) was a close friend of the Prophet (S.A.W) even before Islam. He was known as a gentle and truthful man of Makkah. When the Prophet told him of the revelation, he accepted Islam at once. He is counted with Khadijah (R.A.) and Ali (R.A.) among the earliest converts, and he is remembered as the first free man outside the Prophet's household to believe.

### His role
- He believed immediately. He did not wait to see if the chiefs of Makkah would agree.
- He gave moral support. His calm trust strengthened the Prophet (S.A.W).
- He gave material support. He spent his wealth in the path of Islam.
- He used that wealth to free slaves who were being persecuted for their faith. The freeing of Bilal ibn Rabah (R.A.) is the best-known example. Bilal was tortured for saying that Allah is One, and Abubakar bought his freedom.
- He called other people to Islam and stood with the Prophet when belief was costly.

The earliest converts, taken together, gave the mission its first believers, its first encouragement, its first money, and lives that were ready to bear hardship.

### Appreciating their role
Islam reached later generations because these people held the message at the start. Appreciation is not only a poster of their names. It is:

- Telling the story accurately
- Making dua for them when we remember them
- Volunteering in good Islamic work in the community, such as helping at the mosque or supporting a classmate
- Believing what is true even when friends delay

Khadijah, Ali and Abubakar had different ages and different kinds of help. Each help was needed. A learner's help today may be small, but sincere support of the deen continues their example.

## Key words
• Abubakar (R.A.) — the close friend of the Prophet (S.A.W) and one of the first men to accept Islam
• Bilal (R.A.) — an early Muslim who was freed from slavery; he later gave the call to prayer
• persecution — cruel treatment because of one's faith

## Worked examples

### Example 1
A learner has a little money saved. He wants to copy Abubakar (R.A.). What is a suitable way at Grade 4, and what would not fit?

Working:
1. Abubakar spent wealth to help people harmed for their faith.
2. A child can give a small sadaqah or help someone in need, with a parent's guidance. He cannot copy every adult action.

Answer: He can give a small amount of charity or help a person in need. Showing off, or taking money that is not his, would not follow Abubakar.

## Activity: Roles of the earliest converts
You will need: Notebook, A story of Abubakar (R.A.) from a resource person, course book or digital device
1. Listen to the story of Abubakar (R.A.).
2. Make a table with three names: Khadijah, Ali and Abubakar. Under each name write one role in the Prophet's mission.
3. Discuss, in pairs, why their support mattered at the beginning of Islam.
4. Write one way you can volunteer in a good activity at home, school or the mosque.

## Practice
1. What was the relationship between Abubakar (R.A.) and the Prophet (S.A.W) before Islam?
2. How did Abubakar respond when he heard the message?
3. How did Abubakar help Bilal (R.A.)?
4. Give one way a learner can appreciate the earliest converts.

## Summary
• Abubakar (R.A.) believed at once and supported the mission with loyalty and wealth.
• He freed Muslims who were persecuted, including Bilal (R.A.).
• Khadijah, Ali and Abubakar each gave support that helped Islam begin.

### Answers to practice
1. They were close friends.
2. He accepted Islam at once.
3. He spent his money to free Bilal, who was being persecuted for his faith.
4. Any one: tell their story truthfully, make dua for them, support good Islamic work, or stand by the truth.

questions.question: Who was the first person to accept Islam?
questions.explanation: Khadijah (R.A.) believed the Prophet when he received the first revelation.

questions.question: Which three are the earliest converts studied here?
options: Abu Talib, Abu Lahab and Waraqah
questions.explanation: This sub-strand names Khadijah (R.A.), Ali (R.A.) and Abubakar (R.A.).

questions.question: Why did Khadijah trust Muhammad (S.A.W) before Islam?
questions.explanation: Those qualities led her to propose marriage. People called him Al-Amin.

questions.question: Which support did Khadijah give?
options: She comforted him and supported him with her wealth
questions.explanation: Her role was moral support and material support, and she was the first believer.

questions.question: Ali (R.A.) was…
options: the Prophet's cousin, son of Abu Talib
questions.explanation: He grew up close to the Prophet and accepted Islam while young.

questions.question: What does Ali's early acceptance teach a child?
questions.answer: A young person can believe the truth and stay loyal to it.
questions.explanation: He was still a child when he entered Islam.

questions.question: Abubakar (R.A.) is remembered as…
options: a friend who believed at once and spent his wealth for Islam
a man who refused the message
questions.explanation: He gave both moral and material support.

questions.question: Why is Bilal (R.A.) linked to Abubakar in this lesson?
questions.explanation: Abubakar used his money to free Bilal, who was tortured for his faith.

questions.question: How did the earliest converts help the mission?
questions.answer: Believing first, giving moral and material support, and bearing hardship for the message.
questions.explanation: Their faith, encouragement, wealth and courage carried the mission at the start.

questions.question: A learner appreciates their role by…
options: telling the story truthfully and supporting good work
questions.explanation: Appreciation is shown by truthfulness and by continuing good Islamic effort.
